Engram cells are defined by allocation experiments as a sparse, competitively selected subset of eligible neurons, commonly under twenty to thirty percent of an eligible population in the lateral amygdala, that wins recruitment because of transiently elevated intrinsic excitability driven by the transcription factor CREB.
